subject: chem
title: Redox Reactions & Electrochemistry
syllabus: Electronic concepts of oxidation and reduction, redox reactions, oxidation number, rules for assigning oxidation number, balancing of redox reactions. Electrolytic and metallic conduction, conductance in electrolytic solutions, molar conductivities and their variation with concentration: Kohlrausch's law and its applications. Electrochemical cells — Electrolytic and Galvanic cells, different types of electrodes, electrode potentials including standard electrode potential, half-cell and cell reactions, emf of a Galvanic cell and its measurement: Nernst equation and its applications; Relationship between cell potential and Gibbs' energy change; Dry cell and lead accumulator; Fuel cells.

body: Oxidation = loss of electrons (ON goes UP); reduction = gain of electrons (ON goes DOWN). The oxidising agent is itself reduced.
Rules: element 0; F always −1; O −2 (peroxide −1, superoxide −½, OF_{2} +2); H +1 (metal hydrides −1); the sum equals the charge.
Tricky ones: CrO_{5} and peroxo species keep Cr at +6; Fe_{3}O_{4} gives an average +8/3; the brown-ring complex has Fe +1.
Disproportionation: the SAME element in ONE state goes both up and down — needs an intermediate state (Cl_{2}, H_{2}O_{2}, MnO_{4}^{2−}, Cu^{+}). F_{2} and ClO_{4}^{−} cannot.
Electrons lost = electrons gained. Count the change in ON × number of atoms.
n_{ox} × e_{ox} = n_{red} × e_{red}

body: Galvanic cell: chemical → electrical. Anode = oxidation (−), cathode = reduction (+). Written: anode | ion || ion | cathode.
E°_{cell} = E°_{cathode} − E°_{anode} (both as REDUCTION potentials)
Higher E° → stronger oxidising agent, more easily reduced. A metal displaces another if its E° is lower.
Potentials are intensive: never multiply them by coefficients. To combine half-reactions, add ΔG° = −nFE°: E°_{3} = \f{n_{1}E°_{1} + n_{2}E°_{2}}{n_{1} + n_{2}}.

body: E = E° − \f{0.059}{n} log Q (298 K)
ΔG° = −nFE°, log K = \f{nE°}{0.059}, ΔG = −nFE
Hydrogen electrode: E = −0.059 pH (p_{H_{2}} = 1 bar). Concentration cell: E = \f{0.059}{n} log\f{c_{high}}{c_{low}}.
Metal–insoluble salt electrode: E°(X^{−}/MX/M) = E°(M^{+}/M) + 0.059 log K_{sp}. Calomel: Hg | Hg_{2}Cl_{2} | Cl^{−}.

body: κ falls on dilution (fewer ions per cm^{3}); Λ_{m} rises on dilution.
Strong electrolyte: Λ_{m} = Λ°_{m} − A√{c} (straight line). Weak electrolyte: Λ_{m} shoots up at low c; α = \f{Λ_{m}}{Λ°_{m}}, K = \f{cα^{2}}{1 − α}.
Kohlrausch: Λ° = sum of the ions' λ°. Λ°(CH_{3}COOH) = Λ°(CH_{3}COONa) + Λ°(HCl) − Λ°(NaCl). H^{+} and OH^{−} have the highest λ°.

Cells in series pass the same charge: masses are in the ratio of equivalent masses \f{M}{z}.

Products: cathode takes the species with the higher reduction potential (H_{2} from water for Na^{+}, K^{+}, Mg^{2+}); anode: Cl_{2} from brine, O_{2} from dilute SO_{4}^{2−}/NO_{3}^{−}, S_{2}O_{8}^{2−} from concentrated H_{2}SO_{4}; an active anode (Cu, Ag) itself dissolves.
Brine electrolysis makes OH^{−} (one per electron) — the solution turns basic.
Primary: dry (Leclanché) cell — Zn anode, MnO_{2} cathode (Mn +4 → +3); mercury cell — steady 1.35 V, hearing aids.
Secondary: lead storage (Pb anode, PbO_{2} cathode, 38% H_{2}SO_{4}; both become PbSO_{4} on discharge), Ni–Cd.
H_{2}–O_{2} fuel cell: ~70% efficient, Pt/Pd catalyst, used in Apollo; product is water.
Rusting is electrochemical: Fe anode, O_{2} + H^{+} cathode. Zinc protects even when scratched (sacrificial); tin does not.

traps: Never multiply E° by the coefficients — combine through ΔG° = −nFE° instead.
E°_cell is fixed for a pair of couples; it does not change as the cell runs — E_cell does.
κ DEcreases on dilution while Λ_m INcreases.
In CrO₅ chromium is +6, not +10 (two peroxide groups).
Brine electrolysis gives H₂ at the cathode, never O₂.
Tin coating protects iron only while it is intact; zinc protects even after a scratch.

steps.note: E°, Nernst equation, ΔG and K
Faraday's laws, products, batteries and corrosion

pyq.q: Which of the following reactions are disproportionation reactions? (A) Cu^{+} → Cu^{2+} + Cu (B) 3MnO_{4}^{2−} + 4H^{+} → 2MnO_{4}^{−} + MnO_{2} + 2H_{2}O (C) 2KMnO_{4} → K_{2}MnO_{4} + MnO_{2} + O_{2} (D) 2MnO_{4}^{−} + 3Mn^{2+} + 2H_{2}O → 5MnO_{2} + 4H^{+}. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
sol: Disproportionation: ONE element in ONE oxidation state goes both up and down.
A: Cu(+1) → +2 and 0 ✓. B: Mn(+6) → +7 and +4 ✓. C: Mn is reduced but O is oxidised (two different elements) ✗. D: +7 and +2 meet at +4 — the reverse (comproportionation) ✗.

pyq.q: Lowest oxidation number of an atom in a compound A_{2}B is −2. The number of electrons in its valence shell is
sol: The most negative oxidation number = −(8 − valence electrons).
−2 → 8 − 2 = 6 valence electrons (like O, S).

pyq.q: KMnO_{4} acts as an oxidising agent in acidic medium. 'X' is the difference between the oxidation states of Mn in reactant and product. 'Y' is the number of 'd' electrons present in the brown red precipitate formed at the end of the acetate ion test with neutral ferric chloride. The value of X + Y is ____
sol: Acidic medium: MnO_{4}^{−} (+7) → Mn^{2+} (+2) → X = 5.
The brown-red precipitate is basic iron(III) acetate: Fe^{3+} = 3d^{5} → Y = 5. X + Y = 10.

pyq.q: Consider the following reaction MnO_{2} + KOH + O_{2} → A + H_{2}O. Product 'A' in neutral or acidic medium disproportionate to give products 'B' and 'C' along with water. The sum of spin-only magnetic moment values of B and C is ____ BM. (nearest integer) (Given atomic number of Mn is 25)
Among the following halogens F_{2}, Cl_{2}, Br_{2} and I_{2}, which can undergo disproportionation reaction?
sol: To disproportionate, the element must reach a higher AND a lower state.
F is the most electronegative: it never shows a positive state, so F_{2} cannot. Cl_{2}, Br_{2}, I_{2} can (e.g. X_{2} + 2OH^{−} → X^{−} + XO^{−} + H_{2}O).

pyq.q: Given below are two statements : Statement (I) : The oxidation state of an element in a particular compound is the charge acquired by its atom on the basis of electron gain enthalpy consideration from other atoms in the molecule. Statement (II) : pπ − pπ bond formation is more prevalent in second period elements over other periods. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
sol: Oxidation state is assigned on the basis of ELECTRONEGATIVITY, not electron gain enthalpy → I is incorrect.
Small 2nd-period atoms (C, N, O) overlap p orbitals well → strong pπ–pπ bonds → II is correct.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

Consider the following reactions: NaCl + K_{2}Cr_{2}O_{7} + H_{2}SO_{4} → A + KHSO_{4} + NaHSO_{4} + H_{2}O; A + NaOH → B + NaCl + H_{2}O; B + H_{2}SO_{4} + H_{2}O_{2} → C + Na_{2}SO_{4} + H_{2}O. In the product 'C', 'X' is the number of O_{2}^{2−} units, 'Y' is the total number oxygen atoms present and 'Z' is the oxidation state of Cr. The value of X + Y + Z is _____.
sol: A = CrO_{2}Cl_{2} (chromyl chloride), B = Na_{2}CrO_{4}, C = CrO_{5} (the blue butterfly peroxide).
CrO_{5}: 2 peroxide units, 5 O atoms, Cr = +6 → 2 + 5 + 6 = 13.

pyq.q: The species which does not undergo disproportionation reaction is :
sol: In ClO_{4}^{−}, Cl is already +7 (its maximum) — it can only be reduced, never oxidised.

pyq.q: Element not showing variable oxidation state is :
sol: Fluorine (most electronegative, no d orbitals) shows only −1 in compounds.

pyq.q: From the given list, the number of compounds with +4 oxidation state of Sulphur: SO_{3}, H_{2}SO_{3}, SOCl_{2}, SF_{4}, BaSO_{4}, H_{2}S_{2}O_{7}

In chromyl chloride test for confirmation of Cl^{−} ion, a yellow solution is obtained. Acidification of the solution and addition of amyl alcohol and 10% H_{2}O_{2} turns organic layer blue indicating formation of chromium pentoxide. The oxidation state of chromium in that is
sol: CrO_{5} has one oxide O (−2) and two peroxide groups (−1 each per O): x − 2 − 4 = 0 → x = +6, not +10.

pyq.q: Chlorine undergoes disproportionation in alkaline medium as shown below : a Cl_{2}(g) + b OH^{−}(aq) → c ClO^{−}(aq) + d Cl^{−}(aq) + e H_{2}O(l). The values of a, b, c and d in a balanced redox reaction are respectively :
sol: Cl goes 0 → +1 (ClO^{−}) and 0 → −1 (Cl^{−}): equal numbers.

pyq.q: The oxidation number of iron in the compound formed during brown ring test for NO_{3}^{−} ion is
sol: The brown ring is [Fe(H_{2}O)_{5}(NO)]^{2+}; NO here is NO^{+}.

pyq.q: Alkaline oxidative fusion of MnO_{2} gives "A" which on electrolytic oxidation in alkaline solution produces B. A and B respectively are :
sol: Fusion with KOH + O_{2}/KNO_{3} → green manganate MnO_{4}^{2−} (+6).
Anodic oxidation: MnO_{4}^{2−} → MnO_{4}^{−} + e^{−} (purple permanganate, +7).

pyq.q: Total number of species from the following which can undergo disproportionation reaction _____. H_{2}O_{2}, ClO_{3}^{−}, P_{4}, Cl_{2}, Ag, Cu^{+1}, F_{2}, NO_{2}, K^{+}
sol: Need an intermediate oxidation state: H_{2}O_{2} (−1), ClO_{3}^{−} (+5), P_{4} (0), Cl_{2} (0), Cu^{+} (+1), NO_{2} (+4) → 6.
Ag (no stable negative state), F_{2} (no positive state), K^{+} (cannot be oxidised) cannot.

pyq.q: Given below are two statements : Statement I: S_{8} solid undergoes disproportionation reaction under alkaline conditions to form S^{2−} and S_{2}O_{3}^{2−}. Statement II: ClO_{4}^{−} can undergo disproportionation reaction under acidic condition. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
sol: ClO_{4}^{−} has Cl at +7, the highest state — it cannot disproportionate ✗.
o: Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct
Both statement I and statement II are incorrect
Both statement I and statement II are correct

pyq.q: In the reaction of potassium dichromate, potassium chloride and sulfuric acid (conc.), the oxidation state of the chromium in the product is (+) ____.
sol: The product is CrO_{2}Cl_{2}: x − 4 − 2 = 0 → +6 (the chromyl chloride test is not a redox change for Cr).

pyq.q: The potential for the given half cell at 298 K is (−) ______ × 10^{−2} V. 2H^{+}(aq) + 2e^{−} → H_{2}(g); [H^{+}] = 1 M, P_{H_{2}} = 2 atm (Given: 2.303RT/F = 0.06 V, log 2 = 0.3)
sol: = −0.9 × 10^{−2} V → 1 (nearest integer).

pyq.q: Consider the following electrochemical cell at standard condition: Au(s) | QH_{2}, Q | NH_{4}X(0.01 M) || Ag^{+}(1 M) | Ag(s), E_{cell} = +0.4 V. The couple QH_{2}/Q represents quinhydrone electrode: Q + 2e^{−} + 2H^{+} → QH_{2}, E°_{Q/QH_{2}} = +0.7 V. [Given: E°_{Ag^{+}/Ag} = +0.8 V and \f{2.303RT}{F} = 0.06 V]. The pK_{b} value of the ammonium halide salt (NH_{4}X) used here is ____ (nearest integer)
sol: Anode: QH_{2} → Q (its potential E = 0.7 − 0.06 pH). E_{cell} = 0.8 − (0.7 − 0.06 pH) = 0.4 → pH = 5.
NH_{4}X is a salt of weak base + strong acid: pH = 7 − ½pK_{b} − ½log c = 7 − ½pK_{b} + 1 = 5 → pK_{b} = 6.

pyq.q: The standard cell potential (E°_{cell}) of a fuel cell based on the oxidation of methanol in air that has been used to power television relay station is measured as 1.21 V. The standard half cell reduction potential for O_{2} (E°_{O_{2}/H_{2}O}) is 1.229 V. Choose the correct statement:
sol: O_{2} is reduced at the cathode; methanol is oxidised at the anode; reactants are fed continuously.
o: Oxygen is formed at the anode.
The standard half cell reduction potential for the reduction of CO_{2} (E°_{CO_{2}/CH_{3}OH}) is 19 mV
Reduction of methanol takes place at the cathode.
Reactants are fed at one go to each electrode.

pyq.q: What pressure (bar) of H_{2} would be required to make emf of hydrogen electrode zero in pure water at 25 °C ?
One of the commonly used electrode is calomel electrode. Under which of the following categories calomel electrode comes?
sol: Calomel: Hg | Hg_{2}Cl_{2}(s) | Cl^{−} — a metal, its insoluble salt and the anion of that salt.

pyq.q: For the electro chemical cell M|M^{2+}||X|X^{2−}, if E°_{(M^{2+}/M)} = 0.46 V and E°_{(X/X^{2−})} = 0.34 V, which of the following is correct ?
sol: As written, E_{cell} = E_{right} − E_{left} = 0.34 − 0.46 = −0.12 V → not spontaneous.
So the reverse, M^{2+} + X^{2−} → M + X (E = +0.12 V), is spontaneous.
o: M + X → M^{2+} + X^{2−} is a spontaneous reaction
M^{2+} + X^{2−} → M + X is a spontaneous reaction

pyq.q: How can an electrochemical cell be converted into an electrolytic cell ?
sol: An opposing voltage larger than the cell's own emf drives the reaction backwards — the cell now consumes energy (electrolytic).
o: Applying an external opposite potential greater than E°_{cell}
Reversing the flow of ions in salt bridge.
Applying an external opposite potential lower than E°_{cell}.
Exchanging the electrodes at anode and cathode.

pyq.q: 1 Faraday electricity was passed through Cu^{2+}(1.5 M, 1 L)/Cu and 0.1 Faraday was passed through Ag^{+}(0.2 M, 1 L)/Ag electrolytic cells. After this the two cells were connected (Cu half-cell and Ag half-cell joined by a salt bridge) to make an electrochemical cell. The emf of the cell thus formed at 298 K is ____ mV (nearest integer). Given: E°_{Cu^{2+}/Cu} = 0.34 V, E°_{Ag^{+}/Ag} = 0.8 V, \f{2.303RT}{F} = 0.06 V
sol: 1 F deposits 0.5 mol Cu → [Cu^{2+}] = 1.0 M; 0.1 F deposits 0.1 mol Ag → [Ag^{+}] = 0.1 M.

pyq.q: Given below are two statements : 1 M aqueous solutions of each of Cu(NO_{3})_{2}, AgNO_{3}, Hg_{2}(NO_{3})_{2}; Mg(NO_{3})_{2} are electrolysed using inert electrodes. Given : E°_{Ag^{+}/Ag} = 0.80 V, E°_{Hg_{2}^{2+}/Hg} = 0.79 V, E°_{Cu^{2+}/Cu} = 0.24 V and E°_{Mg^{2+}/Mg} = −2.37 V. Statement (I): With increasing voltage, the sequence of deposition of metals on the cathode will be Ag, Hg and Cu. Statement (II) : Magnesium will not be deposited at cathode instead oxygen gas will be evolved at the cathode. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
sol: Cations with higher E° are reduced first: Ag (0.80) → Hg (0.79) → Cu (0.24) ✓.
Mg^{2+} is not reduced; water is reduced instead — but that gives H_{2} at the cathode, not O_{2} ✗.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect

pyq.q: The emf of cell Tl | Tl^{+} (0.001 M) || Cu^{2+} (0.01 M) | Cu is 0.83 V at 298 K. It could be increased by :
sol: Raising [Cu^{2+}] (reactant) raises E; raising [Tl^{+}] lowers it; scaling both by 10 lowers it (squared term).
o: increasing concentration of both Tl^{+} and Cu^{2+} ions
decreasing concentration of both Tl^{+} and Cu^{2+} ions

pyq.q: The standard reduction potentials at 298 K for the following half cells are given below : Cr_{2}O_{7}^{2−} + 14H^{+} + 6e^{−} → 2Cr^{3+} + 7H_{2}O, E° = 1.33 V; Fe^{3+}(aq) + 3e^{−} → Fe, E° = −0.04 V; Ni^{2+}(aq) + 2e^{−} → Ni, E° = −0.25 V; Ag^{+}(aq) + e^{−} → Ag, E° = 0.80 V; Au^{3+}(aq) + 3e^{−} → Au, E° = 1.40 V. Consider the given electrochemical reactions. The number of metal(s) which will be oxidized be Cr_{2}O_{7}^{2−}, in aqueous solution is ____.
sol: A metal is oxidised if E°_{cell} = 1.33 − E°_{metal} > 0.

pyq.q: An electrochemical cell is constructed using half cells in the direction of spontaneous change: Fe(OH)_{2}(s) + 2e^{−} → Fe(s) + 2OH^{−}(aq), E° = −0.88 V and AgBr(s) + e^{−} → Ag(s) + Br^{−}(aq), E° = +0.07 V. Which of the following option is correct ?
sol: Higher E° (AgBr, +0.07) is the cathode; Fe is oxidised at the anode.
E°_{cell} = 0.07 − (−0.88) = +0.95 V (intensive — it does not double when the equation is doubled).
o: Fe is reduced in the electrochemical cell

pyq.q: Given below are two statements: Statement (I): Oxidising power of halogens decreases in the order F_{2} > Cl_{2} > Br_{2} > I_{2}, which is the basis of "Layer test". Statement (II): "Layer test" to identify Br_{2} and I_{2} in aqueous solution involves the oxidation of bromide or iodide into Br_{2} or I_{2} respectively with Cl_{2}, which is a type of displacement redox reaction. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sol: Cl_{2} (stronger oxidant) displaces Br_{2}/I_{2} from bromide/iodide; the freed halogen colours the organic layer.
Both statements are true.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

If the same buffer was used in the following electrochemical cell to record a cell potential of 235.3 mV, then the value of x = ____ mL (nearest integer). Sn(s) | [Sn(OH)_{6}]^{2−}(0.5 M) | HSnO_{2}^{−}(0.05 M) | OH^{−} | Bi_{2}O_{3}(s) | Bi(s). Consider up to one place of decimal for intermediate calculations. Given: E°_{HSnO_{2}^{−}|Sn(OH)_{6}^{2−}} = −0.9 V, E°_{Bi_{2}O_{3}|Bi} = −0.44 V, pK_{a}(H_{2}CO_{3}) = 6.11, \f{2.303RT}{F} = 0.059 V, antilog(1.29) = 19.5

Consider the following two half-cell reactions along with the standard reduction potential given : CO_{2} + 6H^{+} + 6e^{−} → CH_{3}OH + H_{2}O, E°_{red} = 0.02 V; \f{1}{2}O_{2} + 2H^{+} + 2e^{−} → H_{2}O, E°_{red} = 1.23 V. A fuel cell was set up using the above two half-cell reactions such that the cell operates under the standard condition of 1 bar pressure and 298 K temperature. The fuel cell works with 80% efficiency. If the work derived from the cell using 1 mol of CH_{3}OH is used to compress an ideal gas isothermally against a constant pressure of 1 kPa, then the change in the volume of the gas, ΔV = ____ m^{3}. (nearest integer) Given: F = 96500 C mol^{−1}
sol: Useful work = 80% = 560 472 J = PΔV with P = 1000 Pa → ΔV ≈ 560 m^{3}.

pyq.q: For a closed circuit Daniell cell, which of the following plots is the accurate one at a given temperature? (E°_{cell} on the y-axis, time on the x-axis)
sol: E°_{cell} is the STANDARD potential — a fixed property of the two couples at that temperature.
E_{cell} falls as the cell runs (concentrations change), but E°_{cell} does not: horizontal line.
o: E°_{cell} falls straight to zero at once (vertical drop)
E°_{cell} stays constant — a horizontal line

pyq.q: MX is a sparingly soluble salt that follows the given solubility equilibrium at 298 K: MX(s) ⇌ M^{+}(aq) + X^{−}(aq); K_{sp} = 10^{−10}. If the standard reduction potential for M^{+}(aq) + e^{−} → M(s) is E°_{M^{+}/M} = 0.79 V, then the value of the standard reduction potential for the metal/metal insoluble salt electrode E°_{X^{−}/MX(s)/M} is ____ mV. (nearest integer). [Given: \f{2.303RT}{F} = 0.059 V]

FeO_{4}^{2−} →(+2.0 V) Fe^{3+} →(0.8 V) Fe^{2+} →(−0.5 V) Fe^{0}. In the above diagram, the standard electrode potentials are given in volts (over the arrow). The value of E°_{FeO_{4}^{2−}/Fe^{2+}} is
sol: Potentials do not add — the ΔG° values (−nFE°) do.

pyq.q: Standard electrode potentials for a few half cells are mentioned below : E°_{Cu^{2+}/Cu} = 0.34 V, E°_{Zn^{2+}/Zn} = −0.76 V, E°_{Ag^{+}/Ag} = 0.80 V, E°_{Mg^{2+}/Mg} = −2.37 V. Which one of the following cells gives the most negative value of ΔG° ?
sol: ΔG° = −nFE°_{cell}, n = 2 for each.

pyq.q: For the given cell Fe^{2+}(aq) + Ag^{+}(aq) → Fe^{3+}(aq) + Ag(s), the standard cell potential of the above reaction is (Given: Ag^{+} + e^{−} → Ag, E° = x V; Fe^{2+} + 2e^{−} → Fe, E° = y V; Fe^{3+} + 3e^{−} → Fe, E° = z V)
sol: Fe^{3+} + e^{−} → Fe^{2+}: E° = 3z − 2y (combine ΔG°s).

Consider the following electrochemical cell at 298 K: Pt | HSnO_{2}^{−}(aq) | Sn(OH)_{6}^{2−}(aq) | OH^{−}(aq) | Bi_{2}O_{3}(s) | Bi(s). If the reaction quotient at a given time is 10^{6}, then the cell EMF (E_{cell}) is ____ × 10^{−1} V (Nearest integer). Given the standard half-cell reduction potential as E°_{Bi_{2}O_{3}/Bi, OH^{−}} = −0.44 V and E°_{[Sn(OH)_{6}]^{2−}/HSnO_{2}^{−}, OH^{−}} = −0.90 V
sol: E° = −0.44 − (−0.90) = 0.46 V; balancing 2Bi^{3+}-worth of electrons with 3 Sn: n = 6.

pyq.q: An electrochemical cell consists of the following two redox couples, M^{x+}(aq)/M(s) [E°_{red} = +0.15 V] and Fe^{3+}(aq)/Fe(s) [E°_{red} = −0.036 V]. The cell EMF (E_{cell}) is recorded to be 0.2057 V. If the reaction quotient of the electrochemical reaction is found to be 10^{−2}, then the value of x is ____. (Nearest integer) [Given : M is a p-block metal and \f{2.303RT}{F} = 0.059 V]
sol: n = LCM(x, 3) = 6 with a common p-block ion (Sn^{2+}, Pb^{2+}) → x = 2.

pyq.q: Consider the following electrochemical cell : Pt | O_{2}(g)(1 bar) | HCl(aq) || M^{2+}(aq, 1.0 M) | M(s). The pH above which, oxygen gas would start to evolve at anode is ____ (nearest integer). Given: E°_{M^{2+}/M} = 0.994 V, E°_{O_{2}/H_{2}O} = 1.23 V (standard reduction potentials) and \f{RT}{F}(2.303) = 0.059 V at the given condition
sol: Anode: 2H_{2}O → O_{2} + 4H^{+} + 4e^{−}; its reduction potential is 1.23 − 0.059 pH.
Spontaneous when 0.994 − (1.23 − 0.059 pH) > 0 → pH > 4.

pyq.q: 0.2% (w/v) solution of NaOH is measured to have resistivity 870.0 mΩ m. The molar conductivity of the solution will be ____ × 10^{2} mS dm^{2} mol^{−1}. (Nearest integer)
Correct order of limiting molar conductivity for cations in water at 298 K is :
sol: Small, heavily hydrated Na^{+} moves slower than K^{+}.

pyq.q: The molar conductance of an infinitely dilute solution of ammonium chloride was found to be 185 S cm^{2} mol^{−1} and the ionic conductance of hydroxyl and chloride ions are 170 and 70 S cm^{2} mol^{−1}, respectively. If molar conductance of 0.02 M solution of ammonium hydroxide is 85.5 S cm^{2} mol^{−1}, its degree of dissociation is given by x × 10^{−1}. The value of x is ____ . (Nearest integer)
For a strong electrolyte, a plot of molar conductivity against (concentration)^{1/2} is a straight line, with a negative slope, the correct unit for the slope is

Molar ionic conductivities of divalent cation and anion are 57 S cm^{2} mol^{−1} and 73 S cm^{2} mol^{−1} respectively. The molar conductivity of solution of an electrolyte with the above cation and anion will be
sol: MX (M^{2+}X^{2−}) gives one of each ion: Λ = 57 + 73 = 130 S cm^{2} mol^{−1}.

pyq.q: A conductivity cell with two electrodes (1 cm × 1 cm plates, 1 cm apart, dark side) is half filled with infinitely dilute aqueous solution of a weak electrolyte. If volume is doubled by adding more water at constant temperature, the molar conductivity of the cell will -
sol: At infinite dilution Λ_{m} has already reached its limit Λ°_{m}: further dilution cannot raise it.
Diluting further only lowers the conductance so much that it cannot be measured accurately.
o: remain same or can not be measured accurately

pyq.q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Mohr's salt is composed of only three types of ions-ferrous, ammonium and sulfate. Statement II: If the molar conductance at infinite dilution for ferrous, ammonium and sulfate ions are x_{1}, x_{2} and x_{3} S cm^{2} mol^{−1}, respectively then the molar conductance for Mohr's salt solution at infinite dilution would be given by x_{1} + x_{2} + 2x_{3}. In the light of the given statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
o: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

pyq.q: Which out of the following is a correct equation to show change in molar conductivity with respect to concentration for a weak electrolyte, if the symbols carry their usual meaning :
sol: Ostwald: K_{a} = \f{cα^{2}}{1 − α} with α = \f{Λ_{m}}{Λ_{m}^{°}}.
K_{a}Λ_{m}^{°}(Λ_{m}^{°} − Λ_{m}) = cΛ_{m}^{2} → Λ_{m}^{2}C − K_{a}Λ_{m}^{°2} + K_{a}Λ_{m}Λ_{m}^{°} = 0. (Option 2 is the strong-electrolyte law.)

pyq.q: The molar conductivity for electrolytes A and B are plotted against C^{1/2}: A shoots up steeply (above 400 S cm^{2} mol^{−1}) as C^{1/2} → 0, while B stays almost flat near 200 S cm^{2} mol^{−1}, falling only slightly with concentration. Electrolytes A and B respectively are :
sol: Weak electrolyte: α rises sharply on dilution → Λ_{m} shoots up near zero concentration (A).
Strong electrolyte: already fully ionised → small, linear fall with √{c} (B).

pyq.q: The pH and conductance of a weak acid (HX) was found to be 5 and 4 × 10^{−5} S, respectively. The conductance was measured under standard condition using a cell where the electrode plates having a surface area of 1 cm^{2} were at a distance of 15 cm apart. The value of the limiting molar conductivity is ____ S m^{2} mol^{−1}. (nearest integer) (Given : degree of dissociation of the weak acid (α) << 1)

For strong electrolyte Λ_{m} increases slowly with dilution and can be represented by the equation Λ_{m} = Λ_{m}^{°} − Ac^{1/2}. Molar conductivity values of the solutions of strong electrolyte AB at 18 °C are: c (mol L^{−1}) = 0.04, 0.09, 0.16, 0.25 with Λ_{m} (S cm^{2} mol^{−1}) = 96.1, 95.7, 95.3, 94.9. The value of constant A based on the above data [in S cm^{2} mol^{−1}/(mol/L)^{1/2}] unit is ____ .

Given below is the plot of the molar conductivity vs √{concentration} for KCl in aqueous solution: it is a straight line passing through Λ_{m} = 150 S cm^{2} mol^{−1} at √{C} = 0.1 and Λ_{m} = 100 S cm^{2} mol^{−1} at √{C} = 0.15 (mol/L)^{1/2}. If, for the higher concentration of KCl solution, the resistance of the conductivity cell is 100 Ω, then the resistance of the same cell with the dilute solution is 'x' Ω. The value of x is ____ (Nearest integer)
The molar conductivity of a weak electrolyte when plotted against the square root of its concentration, which of the following is expected to be observed ?
sol: α falls rapidly as a weak electrolyte gets more concentrated → Λ_{m} drops sharply (and rises steeply on dilution).
o: A small decrease in molar conductivity is observed at infinite dilution.
A small increase in molar conductivity is observed at infinite dilution.
Molar conductivity increases sharply with increase in concentration.
Molar conductivity decreases sharply with increase in concentration.

pyq.q: Identify the factor from the following that does not affect electrolytic conductance of a solution.
sol: Conductance depends on the electrolyte, its concentration, the solvent (viscosity, dielectric) and temperature — not on what the electrodes are made of.
o: The nature of the electrolyte added.
The nature of the electrode used.

pyq.q: A solution of aluminium chloride is electrolysed for 30 minutes using a current of 2 A. The amount of the aluminium deposited at the cathode is ____ . [Given : molar mass of aluminium and chlorine are 27 g mol^{−1} and 35.5 g mol^{−1} respectively. Faraday constant = 96500 C mol^{−1}]
Which of the following electrolyte can be used to obtain H_{2}S_{2}O_{8} by the process of electrolysis?
sol: With concentrated H_{2}SO_{4}, HSO_{4}^{−} is oxidised at the anode: 2HSO_{4}^{−} → H_{2}S_{2}O_{8} + 2e^{−}.
Dilute solutions give O_{2} at the anode instead.
o: Acidified dilute solution of sodium sulphate.

pyq.q: Electrolysis of 600 mL aqueous solution of NaCl for 5 min changes the pH of the solution to 12. The current in Amperes used for the given electrolysis is ____ . (Nearest integer).

A constant current was passed through a solution of AuCl_{4}^{−} ion between gold electrodes. After a period of 10.0 minutes, the increase in mass of cathode was 1.314 g. The total charge passed through the solution is ____ × 10^{−2} F. (Given atomic mass of Au = 197)

O_{2} gas will be evolved as a product of electrolysis of : (A) an aqueous solution of AgNO_{3} using silver electrodes. (B) an aqueous solution of AgNO_{3} using platinum electrodes. (C) a dilute solution of H_{2}SO_{4} using platinum electrodes. (D) a high concentration solution of H_{2}SO_{4} using platinum electrodes. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sol: Silver anode dissolves (Ag → Ag^{+}) instead of making O_{2} → A ✗.
Inert Pt with NO_{3}^{−} or dilute SO_{4}^{2−}: water is oxidised → O_{2} (B ✓, C ✓). Concentrated H_{2}SO_{4} gives S_{2}O_{8}^{2−} → D ✗.

pyq.q: One Faraday of electricity liberates x × 10^{−1} gram atom of copper from copper sulphate, x is ____ .
sol: Cu^{2+} + 2e^{−} → Cu: 2 F per mol → 1 F gives 0.5 gram atom = 5 × 10^{−1}.

pyq.q: Fuel cell, using hydrogen and oxygen as fuels, A. has been used in spaceship B. has as efficiency of 40% to produce electricity C. uses aluminium as catalysts D. is eco-friendly E. is actually a type of Galvanic cell only
sol: H_{2}–O_{2} fuel cells powered the Apollo missions (A ✓), make only water (D ✓) and are galvanic cells (E ✓).
Efficiency is about 70% (B ✗); catalysts are finely divided Pt or Pd (C ✗).

pyq.q: The reaction at cathode in the cells commonly used in clocks involves.
sol: Dry (Leclanché) cell cathode: MnO_{2} + NH_{4}^{+} + e^{−} → MnO(OH) + NH_{3}: Mn +4 → +3.

pyq.q: Match List I with List II. List-I (Cell): A. Leclanche cell, B. Ni-Cd cell, C. Fuel cell, D. Mercury cell. List-II (Use/Property/Reaction): I. Converts energy of combustion into electrical energy, II. Does not involve any ion in solution and is used in hearing aids, III. Rechargeable, IV. Reaction at anode Zn → Zn^{2+} + 2e^{−}. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
sol: Leclanché: Zn → Zn^{2+} + 2e^{−} at the anode (IV). Ni–Cd: rechargeable (III).
Fuel cell: combustion energy → electricity (I). Mercury cell: paste electrolyte, no ions in solution, used in hearing aids (II).

pyq.q: Which of the following statements is not correct about rusting of iron?
sol: Tin is LESS reactive than iron: once the coating breaks, iron becomes the anode and rusts even faster (unlike zinc, which protects sacrificially).
o: Coating of iron surface by tin prevents rusting, even if the tin coating is peeling off.
When pH lies above 9 or 10, rusting of iron does not take place.
Dissolved acidic oxides SO_{2}, NO_{2} in water act as catalyst in the process of rusting.
Rusting of iron is envisaged as setting up of electrochemical cell on the surface of iron object.

pyq.q: Match List-I with List-II. List-I (Applications): (A) Transistors, (B) Hearing aids, (C) Invertors, (D) Apollo space ship. List-II (Batteries/Cell): (I) Anode − Zn/Hg; Cathode − HgO + C, (II) Hydrogen fuel cell, (III) Anode - Zn; Cathode - Carbon, (IV) Anode - Pb; Cathode − Pb | PbO_{2}. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sol: Transistors → dry cell (Zn/C, III); hearing aids → mercury cell (I); invertors → lead storage battery (IV); Apollo → H_{2}–O_{2} fuel cell (II).
